summary: The 17-item test split influenced three Phase 2 decisions. It remains usable for model-vs-human quality agreement (no labels exist, and no prompt, rubric or aggregation was tuned on test outputs). It is NOT a clean hold-out for the components listed below; use real_holdout@v2 for confirmatory claims about them.

exposures.what_was_seen: Classifier outputs on all 29 pilot items, test split included (21/29 interview_podcast; 0/7 Talk Python).
exposures.decision_influenced: Speaker-turn format cue and interview_podcast genre were designed with the pilot format in view.
affected_claims: genre accuracy / macro-F1 on real content

exposures.what_was_seen: v1 flagged 5/29 pilot episodes (test split included) and 24/104 other episodes; v2 patterns were written from those false positives.
affected_claims: the '24/104 -> 1/104 held-out' figure: those 104 episodes informed the design, so they are development data, not a hold-out

exposures.what_was_seen: nDCG@5 of both embedders on the 17 test items with topical proxy labels.
exposures.decision_influenced: Keeping hashing as the recommendation default (docs cite the test-split result).
affected_claims: any confirmatory claim that one embedder recommends better

not_exposed: LLM rubric prompts and rubric anchors (no live model was run on any pilot item)
Aggregation weights and genre profiles (not changed in response to test outputs)
Release gate thresholds (locked before any annotation; unchanged)
